text:
Dense, eternal mist, so I may forget where
the brine wave of the sea cast me ashore.
The land I came to has no spring;
it has a long night that hides me like a mother.

The wind circles my house with sobs
and cries, and breaks my shout like glass.
On the white plain, whose horizon has no end,
I watch intense, painful sunsets die.

Whom can she call, who has come this far,
when only the dead have gone farther?
They alone behold a silent, lifeless sea
growing between their arms and their loved ones' arms!

The ships, their sails white in the harbor,
come from lands where none of mine are;
their fair-eyed men know not my rivers,
and bring pale fruit without my orchards' light.

The question rising to my throat
falls back defeated as I watch them pass:
they speak strange tongues, not the moved tongue
my poor mother sings in lands of gold.

I watch the snow descend like dust on a grave;
the mist grow like one who is dying;
and, lest I go mad, I cannot find the moments,
for the long night has only just begun.

I gaze at the entranced plain and gather its grief,
which comes to see the mortal landscapes.
Snow is the face appearing at my windows:
its whiteness will always descend from heaven!

Always it, silent as God's great gaze upon me;
always its blossom over my house; always,
like fate that neither wanes nor passes,
it will descend to cover me, terrible and entranced.

translation.title: Desolation
